newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian municipalities sell 13.5 pct of Dexia CC.
newsitem.headline: Belgian municipalities sell 13.5 pct of Dexia CC.

text.p: Holding Communal, a holding company 100 percent owned by Belgium's municipalities, said on Wednesday it had decided to sell 13.5 percent more of its Dexia Belgium shares in the market through a global offering.
Dexia Belgium, 65.5 percent owned by Holding Communal, owns 50 percent of Belgian bank Credit Communal/Gemeentekrediet (CCB) and 50 percent of French Credit Local de France.
The transaction consists of a public offering to Belgian retail investors of 2,474,228 shares and 2,474,229 shares to institutional investors in Belgium and abroad.
The combined offering totals 4,948,457 shares or about 13.5 percent of the company's outstanding share capital.
Holding Communal has granted an option to purchase up to 742,268 ordinary shares for the purpose of covering over-allotments if any.
A maximum price will be announced in connection with the Belgian retail offering on June 14.
The final offer price for the whole of the combined offering will be set following a bookbuilding process and will be confirmed in the week of June 23.
Dexia Belgium shares are expected to be listed on the Brussels stock exchange and to be quoted on SEAQ International in London.
Morgan Stanley Dean Witter is global coordinator and book runner for the combined offering.
